pr.title: Add `SingleUseConsts` mir-opt pass
pr.description:
The goal here is to make a pass that can be run in debug builds to simplify the common case of constants that are used just once -- that doesn't need SSA handling and avoids any potential downside of multi-use constants.  In particular, to simplify the `if T::IS_ZST` pattern that's common in the standard library.

By also handling the case of constants that are *never* actually used this fully replaces the `ConstDebugInfo` pass, since it has all the information needed to do that naturally from the traversal it needs to do anyway.

This is roughly a wash on instructions on its own (a couple regressions, a few improvements https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/125910#issuecomment-2144963361), with a bunch of size improvements.  So I'd like to land it as its own PR, then do follow-ups to take more advantage of it (in the inliner, cg_ssa, etc).

r? @saethlin
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR does not describe a semantics-changing wrong transformation. The superseded ConstDebugInfo pass only rewrote debug-info places from a constant-assigned local to the constant, while the new SingleUseConsts pass additionally replaces the single constant use with the same constant and turns the initialization into nop. Those are standard const-substitution steps guarded by exactly one constant initialization, at most one operand use, and exclusion of arguments/return place and all other place contexts. The only observable changes in the patch are MIR shape and debug-info representation, neither of which yields a different deterministic runtime value. Constructing a differing pair would require an unrelated return-value change or violating the pass preconditions, which the task forbids.

analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical `ConstDebugInfo` behavior was an incomplete transformation rather than a semantic miscompile: it left `_l = const C` in place and only rewrote debug info, so downstream passes and codegen still saw an indirect temporary for single-use constants. The new transformation instead turns the initialization into `nop` and puts the constant directly at the one use (for example `switchInt(const <T as MyTrait>::ASSOC_BOOL)`), and for never-used locals removes the assignment while preserving debuginfo as `debug my_int => const <T as MyTrait>::ASSOC_INT`. The important correctness boundary is that this substitution must NOT be generalized to function arguments/return place or to multi-use locals: the pass only removes constants with a single use because re-evaluating constants is not always an improvement, especially for large ones.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR functions containing a local assigned from a constant (`Rvalue::Use(Operand::Constant)`), especially generic associated constants used in `if`/`match`; runs when `sess.mir_opt_level() > 0`, with both panic=abort and panic=unwind, and with `-C debuginfo=full` to exercise debug-info rewriting.
analysis.originalLogic: MIR building creates temporaries for common patterns such as `if T::IS_ZST`, `if CONST`, and `match CONST`, so the constant is first assigned to a local and then read. The pre-existing `ConstDebugInfo` pass only found locals assigned once to a constant and otherwise used only by debuginfo, then changed `VarDebugInfoContents::Place` to `Const`; it did not propagate the constant into a real single use or erase the initialization. The PR describes the old pass as fully replaced: "By also handling the case of constants that are *never* actually used this fully replaces the `ConstDebugInfo` pass".
pitfalls: Do not treat `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` as uses or as a second initialization; the pass explicitly skips them.

Do not rewrite an argument local even if it is assigned a constant. The `keep_parameter` test expects `_1 = const <T as MyTrait>::ASSOC_INT;` to remain because `_1` is within the argument range; assigning the argument is a real mutation, unlike initializing a temporary.
The return place `_0` is also in the excluded argument range, which is why `assign_const_to_return` is unchanged (`_0 = const <T as MyTrait>::ASSOC_BOOL;`).
Do not propagate a constant into multiple uses; the PR deliberately restricts to single-use to avoid re-evaluating large constants.
When deleting the initialization, simple debug info must be updated from the local to the constant, otherwise the debug value points at a local whose definition is now `nop`.
The `LocalReplacer` must consume exactly one operand; a second matching use is treated as a compiler bug (`"there was a second use of the operand"`), reflecting the finder's single-use invariant.
The old `ConstDebugInfo` was first gated with `// Disabled in favour of `SingleUseConsts`` and `sess.mir_opt_level() > 2`, then deleted; `SingleUseConsts` uses `sess.mir_opt_level() > 0`.

Downstream pass dumps (`DestinationPropagation`, `GVN`, `SimplifyComparisonIntegral`, `Inline`) change because their inputs now contain direct constants and `nop`s; those test updates do not by themselves indicate a bug in those passes.
preconditions: The local must not be an argument or return place: `finder.ineligible_locals.insert_range(..=Local::from_usize(body.arg_count));`
More than one constant initialization makes the local ineligible: `if locations.init_loc.is_some() { self.ineligible_locals.insert(local); }`
More than one operand use makes the local ineligible: `if locations.use_loc.is_some() { self.ineligible_locals.insert(local); }`
Storage markers are ignored and do not count as uses: `StatementKind::StorageLive(_) | StatementKind::StorageDead(_) => {}` with the comment `// Storage markers are irrelevant to this.`
Any unexpected place context marks the local ineligible: `// If there's any path that gets here, rather than being understood elsewhere,` and `// then we'd better not do anything with this local.`
Simple debug-info places are tracked for rewriting, while other debug-info contents go through `super_var_debug_info` and therefore make the local ineligible.
The single use must actually be found by the replacer: `"operand wasn't used replacing local {local:?} with locations {locations:?} in body {body:#?}"`.
analysis.summary: Adds the `SingleUseConsts` MIR pass, which finds a non-argument local initialized by `_l = const C` and used at most once, substitutes `C` at that single use, and replaces the initialization with `nop`; it also handles never-used constant locals and rewrites simple debug-info places to the constant. The pass supersedes and later deletes the narrower `ConstDebugInfo` pass.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `//@ test-mir-pass: SingleUseConsts`, `//@ compile-flags: -C debuginfo=full`, and `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY` to check both panic strategies. Define a `trait MyTrait { const ASSOC_BOOL: bool; const ASSOC_INT: i32; }` so constants are not locally folded. Add focused functions: `if_const`/`match_const` expecting `switchInt(const <T as MyTrait>::ASSOC_BOOL/INT)` and the init becoming `nop`; `if_const_debug`/`match_const_debug` with an intervening `do_whatever()` call and a debug local, expecting `debug my_bool => const ...` plus a still-indirect `_3 = const ...` for the `if` temporary; `never_used_debug` expecting the init to become `nop` while debug info becomes `debug my_int => const ...`; `assign_const_to_return` expecting `_0 = const ...` to remain; and `keep_parameter` expecting `_1 = const ...` to remain. Also check the old `ConstDebugInfo` test is converted to `SingleUseConsts` and that only the pass name and emitted MIR change.
analysis.trigger: A local `_l` is initialized exactly once by `_l = const C`, is not a function argument (nor the return place covered by the argument range), has at most one subsequent operand use, and is not reached by any other place/context visitor path; alternatively the local has zero uses after the initialization.
